intended_object: The standard bijection, for n ≠ 0, between isomorphism classes of regular permutation triples (regular dessins/hypermaps) of degree n with component orders dividing a, b, c and normal subgroups of index n of the triangle group Δ(a,b,c). A normal subgroup N goes to the class of the action on Δ/N, and a class goes to the kernel of its monodromy representation. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the cited references (Girondo–González-Diez Prop. 2.66, Jones–Singerman).
explanation: The equivalence inverts the map that sends a normal subgroup N of index n to the class of its coset triple (the action of Δ(a,b,c) on Δ(a,b,c)/N, with the cosets numbered by Fin n); that map is proved bijective. The companion lemmas confirm the inverse direction is the kernel of the representation. The ingredients are the standard notions: TriangleGroup is the presented group ⟨x,y,z | xᵃ, yᵇ, zᶜ, xyz⟩; IsRegular means connected with an automorphism group acting transitively on the sheets; HasDividingOrders means σ0ᵃ = σ1ᵇ = σinfᶜ = 1; and IsoClass is the quotient by relabeling. The hypothesis NeZero n is needed: with n = 0 there are no regular triples, while Subgroup.index = 0 picks out the normal subgroups of infinite index, so the two sides would differ. The setting (triangle groups and permutation triples) is the one in which this correspondence is stated in the literature, so it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no triangle groups and no such correspondence.
